item.title: New Jersey Drops Coinbase Staking Order After Three Years
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine New Jersey Drops Coinbase Staking Order After Three Years New Jersey’s securities regulator has withdrawn the 2023 cease-and-desist order that barred Coinbase from offering staking to new customers in the state, ending a three-year standoff that cost residents an estimated $15 million in forgone rewards. The Bureau of Securities notice , dated Oct. 30 and signed by Acting Bureau Chief Keith A. Alt, rescinds the order and the $5 million penalty that came with it. The withdrawal is without prejudice and without a ruling on the merits. Coinbase disclosed the development in its third-quarter report filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which states that the regulator informed the company of its intent to rescind on Oct. 29. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said New Jersey users would regain access to staking “very soon.” As of Monday, the exchange’s eligibility page continued to list New Jersey among the states where customers cannot stake new principal, and no reopening date has been announced. How the staking case began The order traces to June 6, 2023, when the New Jersey bureau joined securities regulators in nine other states — Alabama, California, Illinois, Kentucky, Maryland, South Carolina, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin — in a coordinated action against Coinbase’s staking program. The states alleged the service amounted to an unregistered securities offering under state law. California led the task force; its action covered more than 600,000 accounts. In July 2023, Coinbase agreed with California, New Jersey, South Carolina and Wisconsin to block customers in those states from staking new funds pending final adjudication. Maryland reached a similar agreement in October 2023. Customers who had staked before the orders kept earning rewards, but could not add principal or compound the rewards they received. The state cases ran parallel to the SEC’s June 2023 lawsuit against Coinbase, which named staking among its claims. The SEC dismissed that case in February 2025. Alabama, Kentucky, Illinois, South Carolina and Vermont dismissed, vacated or withdrew their own actions in March and April 2025. New Jersey is the sixth of the original ten states to step back. What the withdrawal does and does not do Rescinding the order ends the restriction on new staking in New Jersey. It does not resolve the underlying legal question. The bureau made no finding on whether Coinbase’s staking program is a security, and the “without prejudice” language preserves its ability to file a new action. Coinbase’s own filing calls the state matters “preliminary” and says an adverse resolution “could have a material impact” on the business. The filing describes a planned rescission rather than a completed one, which explains the gap between Armstrong’s statement and the unchanged eligibility page. item.title: Report: OKC Thunder add Dalen Terry to 15th NBA roster spot
item.description: The Oklahoma City Thunder have filled their final roster standard spot. They have reportedly signed Dalen Terry to a two-year deal, per ESPN's Shams Charania. After a little bit of an adventure with the No. 15 spot, they finally land on a guy. Terry has played the last four seasons in the NBA. He was the No. 18 pick of the 2022 NBA draft. He spent the first three-plus years with the Chicago Bulls before finishing last season with the Philadelphia 76ers . The 24-year-old has averaged 3.5 points on 44.3% shooting, 1.7 rebounds and 1.2 assists in his career. After the Thunder lost Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace for the foreseeable future — and maybe for the entire 2026-27 season for the latter two — they had to fill in the vacant roster spot. Leaving it open was a luxury they couldn't afford any longer. As mentioned earlier, it's been quite the ride to get to this point. The Thunder had previously signed Ochai Agbaji to a standard roster spot deal this past Friday. And then OKC backed out of it on Saturday. They had to recalibrate after learning Holmgren will miss two-plus months with a torn patellar tendon. Now, Terry joins the Thunder. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led them to a much-needed win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday. But they still badly need NBA-capable bodies to fill out their rotation. The hope is that he can be one of those guys. G/F Dalen Terry has agreed on a two-year deal with the Oklahoma City Thunder, sources tell ESPN. Terry enters his fifth NBA season after the former No. overall 18 pick spent time in Chicago and Philadelphia, and went to training camp with Golden State last month. pic.twitter.com/JlVzvyRcC4 — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) November 3, 2026 This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Report: OKC Thunder add Dalen Terry to 15th NBA roster spot

item.title: WWE 'Raw': John Cena details 'John Cena Classic' event, debuts new championship
item.description: WWE star John Cena (R) and his wife Shay Shariatzadeh attend the premiere of "Coyote vs. Acme" in Los Angeles on August 26, 2026. Cena detailed the upcoming John Cena Classic event in on WWE "Raw." Photo by Jim Ruymen/UPI Nov. 3 (UPI) -- Retired WWE star John Cena returned to Raw on Monday to detail the upcoming John Cena Classic event and debuted a new championship. Cena arrived in a new "Never Give Up" t-shirt and told the live audience in New York City that he actually had three big announcements concerning the event. First, the John Cena Classic will take place on December 14 from Disney World in Orlando. The event, a tournament that features WWE wrestlers taking on the stars of tomorrow from NXT, will be presented on a second edition of Raw with the first coming live from Perth, Australia. Cena then unveiled the new John Cena Classic Championship belt. The championship, which will be granted to the winner of the tournament, features Cena's logo and pay homage to his classic spinner belt. Cody Rhodes was then introduced as the first participant in the tournament for the final announcement. John Cena (L) and his wife Shay Shariatzadeh arrive on the red carpet for the premiere of "Happy Gilmore 2" in New York City on July 21, 2025. Photo by John Angelillo/UPI Future participants will be voted on by fans who are members of Club WWE, a recently launched paid membership program that offers deals on tickets and exclusive merchandise, among other perks.

item.title: Browns’ Spencer Fano Issues a Critical Take After Deshaun Watson’s 8-Sack Game Against The Steelers
item.description: The Cleveland Browns have issues to fix after losing badly to their AFC North Division rivals Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Cleveland had an awful outing versus the Steelers, and that can be said in particular about the team’s offensive line, which didn’t do a great job at protecting quarterback Deshaun Watson. The Steelers sacked the former Clemson Tigers star signal-caller eight times for a loss of 41 yards for the Browns. Cleveland ended that game absorbing a 27-6 loss, as the Steelers successfully returned the favor weeks after their loss in Cleveland. Following the game, Cleveland offensive tackle Spencer Fano admitted that he had a subpar performance in Week 8. “I need to play a whole lot better than what I put out on that field,” the rookie said, via Camryn Justice of News 5 Cleveland . “I feel like I’ve been taking steps all season, and feel like I took a little step back today and just need to get better.” #Browns T Spencer Fano was not happy with his performance in today's loss to the Steelers: "I need to play a whole lot better than what I put out on that field." "I feel like I've been taking steps all season, and feel like I took a little step back today and just need to get… pic.twitter.com/jBrTnvMVg4 — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) November 1, 2026 Browns Rookie Fano Can Bounce Back in Week 8 Game in The Big Easy May 8, 2026; Berea, OH, USA; Cleveland tackle Fano (55) blocks defensive end Logan Fano (97) during rookie minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images The 21-year-old Fano was selected in the first round (ninth overall) by Cleveland in the 2026 NFL Draft, so there is surely a lot for him to learn in the pros. But the lack of experience at this level of football can’t also be a total excuse for bad play. Fano received great reviews for his Week 7 play against the Tennessee Titans , and he’ll look to return to that form when Cleveland visits the New Orleans Saints for a Week 9 matchup this coming Sunday at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans. Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) walks off the field after losing to the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. item.title: Why Alexander Zverev’s rise to world No 1 rings hollow
item.description: This Monday, when the ATP tennis rankings were updated, there was a new name at the top of the list. Alexander Zverev has capped the best year of his life by ascending to world No 1 for the first time, at the conclusion of a season in which the 29-year-old finally ended his grand slam drought with two titles. It has been an excellent year for one of tennis’s most consistent athletes, who has been a fixture in and around the top 10 since 2017. On paper, the German’s story is one of triumph over adversity, of the extraordinary difficulty of managing type 1 diabetes with life as an elite athlete and not letting health conditions inhibit one’s sporting dreams. He overcame a debilitating ankle injury sustained in the French Open semi-finals in 2022, which left him needing to be helped off court in a wheelchair. Then there are the infamous slam finals, the total and utter implosions from two-sets-to-love up and two-sets-to-one up against Dominic Thiem and Carlos Alcaraz respectively at the US Open 2020 and Roland-Garros 2024. He overcame that psychological turmoil too , finally breaking his duck at the French Open this year. But Zverev’s ascent to the top of the sport in many ways feels hard to celebrate. The feelgood story summarised above, of resilience and discipline, is all true. Yet, if true, other stories about his history and character may make it ring hollow to many observers uncomfortable with his continued presence in the sport at all. He has been accused by two former partners of domestic abuse , allegations which Zverev adamantly denies. Olga Sharypova made allegations of physical and emotional abuse against him in interviews with Racquet magazine in 2020 and Slate in 2021, but did not bring a court action, insisting she only wanted to share her story and to inspire women in similar situations to come forward. Zverev settled out of court with another ex-partner , Brenda Patea, in 2024, after he had previously been issued a penalty order – which occurs under German law where the evidence for one side is considered compelling and a trial deemed unnecessary – and fined. The court was clear in its statement after the 2024 settlement: “The decision is not a verdict and it is not a decision about guilt or innocence.” Zverev has since inaccurately claimed it proved his innocence. He has not been convicted. There has been no verdict at all, leaving him in a limbo state, a grey space with no legally definitive outcome but where the harrowing details of the accusations cannot be forgotten by those who have read them. He is obviously not the first sportsman to be in this position, nor will he be the last. That does not detract from the severity of what he has been accused of and the inability of many tennis viewers to, in good conscience, support him. item.title: 'It's too early': Sachin Tendulkar cautions against giving Vaibhav Sooryavanshi key role
item.description: 'It's too early': Sachin Tendulkar cautions against giving Vaibhav Sooryavanshi key role originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India great Sachin Tendulkar said it is too early for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to be a Duleep Trophy vice-captain. Sooryavanshi hit 92 off 81 balls against Central Zone and narrowly missed Tendulkar’s record. He led East Zone in the semi-final after Ishan Kishan injured his hand. Sachin Tendulkar advises patience over Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's leadership role It may be too early, in the opinion of Sachin Tendulkar, to hand Vaibhav Sooryavanshi a major leadership role in red-ball cricket, and the batting great made that clear when a fan raised the subject during an interactive question-and-answer session. The 15-year-old has taken Indian cricket by storm over the past year, and his rapid progress has led many to wonder how quickly he should be given extra responsibility. He was, in fact, named vice-captain for East Zone during the recently concluded Duleep Trophy. He was even in charge of East Zone for a stretch of their Duleep Trophy semi-final against Central Zone. Tendulkar appeared to believe that the teenager’s priority should be on batting and nothing else for now. He explained that Sooryavanshi needs a larger number of red-ball matches under his belt before anyone starts thinking about added duties. “I feel it’s too early for him to become a vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy,” Tendulkar said. “We have to let him play more matches with the red ball and take one step at a time!” Nonetheless, the teenager does have some experience in a leadership role as he was vice-captain of Bihar in last season’s Ranji Trophy, and earlier this year he held the same post in the India Under-19 team that lifted the World Cup. MORE: Youngest captain in first-class cricket: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi acts as stand-in skipper in Duleep Trophy semi-final as Ishan Kishan suffers injury Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s Duleep Trophy 2026 performances for East Zone On the field, the youngster has given plenty of reasons for the excitement around him. In the semi-final against Central Zone on August 30, he smashed 92 off 81 balls, which made him the youngest half-centurion in the history of the Duleep Trophy. He came close to going one step further as well, since he narrowly missed beating Tendulkar’s 36-year-old record as the youngest first-class centurion in the competition. item.title: Afrique Femme & CANEX WKND 2026 Partner to Celebrate Francophone Fashion, Culture, and Female Leadership in Lagos
item.description: From November 5 to 8, 2026 , Lagos will become the epicenter of African creativity as Afrique Femme brings the 6th edition of the Week-end des African Woman 2.0 Brunch to CANEX WKND 2026 at the iconic Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture & Creative Arts. Organized by Afreximbank in collaboration with the African Union and the AfCFTA Secretariat, Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX WKND) is Africa’s premier event celebrating the continent’s creative and cultural industries. Under the overarching theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World: From FESTAC ’77 to CANEX ’27,” this year’s gathering will connect thousands of creative entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers, and cultural icons from across Global Africa and the diaspora. Spotlighting Francophone Luxury & Made-in-Africa Fashion As part of this landmark event, Afrique Femme is hosting a dedicated Exhibition Pavilion designed to bridge Francophone and Anglophone creative ecosystems. The pavilion will feature curated showcases, pop-ups, and private sales from leading West and Central African designers. Attendees will experience exclusive collections from celebrated brands including Makeda by AYA Konan ,, KUMI , KWELAKU , and Galipette Atelier , highlighting the richness, craftsmanship, and global potential of Francophone fashion. The African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch A core highlight of the week will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026 , with the African Woman 2.0 VIP Networking Brunch . Bringing together 200 to 250 influential women leaders, policymakers, innovators, and international dignitaries, the high-level gathering will feature keynote addresses, strategic panels, and structured B2B networking aimed at fostering female leadership and economic empowerment across the continent. “We are thrilled to bring the African Woman 2.0 platform to Lagos alongside CANEX WKND 2026,” said Aïssata Sidibé N’DIA , Managing Director of RED Côte d’Ivoire / Afrique Femme. “This partnership offers an extraordinary opportunity to celebrate the ingenuity of African creative entrepreneurs, showcase Francophone fashion excellence on a global stage, and build lasting cross-border trade and investment synergies across Africa.” Event & Registration Details Dates: November 5–8, 2026 Venue: Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture & Creative Arts (National Theatre), Lagos, Nigeria Registration: Delegate attendance at CANEX WKND 2026 is 100% free , but pre-registration is mandatory. Visitors are invited to register at wknd.canex.africa , select “Visitor / Delegate,” and indicate “Afrique Femme” under referral source. About Afrique Femme AfriqueFemme.com is a leading Pan-African digital media platform produced by Weblogy Group. Dedicated to inspiring, educating, and empowering African women, Afrique Femme reaches millions of readers and viewers monthly across West Africa and the global diaspora through high-impact editorial content, TV shows, and flagship events such as the Week-end des African Woman 2.0 . item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. item.title: ‘Somebody’s going to get the blame’: Von Miller points the finger elsewhere after Cowboys loss
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images On Sunday, the Dallas Cowboys fell to the Arizona Cardinals, leaving fans utterly shocked by the unraveling. The overtime thriller ended with a Cardinals field goal to seal the 33-30 win, and another loss for the Cowboys’ disappointing season. For the fifth consecutive time, the Cardinals have defeated the Cowboys on their home turf, marking a 5-0 record at AT&T Stadium. The latest loss has led to a lot of criticism for the coaching staff, especially head coach Brian Schottenheimer. But after the game, veteran linebacker Von Miller came to their defense a bit. The Comeback Down 30-24, Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew rallied the team late in the fourth quarter, ultimately finding wide receiver Michael Wilson in the back of the end zone with seconds left on the clock. Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland lined up for a normal extra point but missed left, leaving the score tied and Cowboys fans relieved. To start overtime, both teams failed to find field goal range until the Cardinals put their second and final possession to use. After a Wilson 17-yard catch and a Tyler Allegier run for 11 yards, Ryland found a comfortable position for redemption and sealed a 33-30 victory. Dallas led by two touchdowns early in the fourth quarter but crumbled in the last 16 minutes of regulation. Veterans Speak Up Nothing new for longtime Cowboys players and fans, especially linebacker Von Miller, but after the loss, the 16-year veteran gave a balanced response, defending the coaching staff for any blame that may come as a result. “I’m a parent,” Miller said, via Jon Machota of The Athletic . “I got three kids. Sometimes you raise your kids a certain way, and you teach them lessons. You expect them to act a certain way when they go out. “And sometimes the kids just go out there and do things that are not a reflection of who you are as a parent. And I use that reference for our coaching staff. We have amazing coaches that keep us prepared, ready to go mentally, physically, emotionally. They breathe life into us, and just for whatever reason, that’s the product. “The product that went out there is not a reflection of our coaching staff. This is pro sports. This is not parenting. So at the end of the day, the buck has to stop somewhere. Somebody’s going to get the blame. “But my opinion, this is just me, I don’t know nothing about football. I only played 16 years. We’ve got great coaches. We’ve got a great coaching staff. And that’s not a reflection of how they coach us and get us ready every week.” Despite the apt analogy, Miller failed to realize that paid athletes, like in any professional field, have expectations, and if not met, repercussions follow. The Cowboys haven’t had a Super Bowl season since 1996, and most sports enthusiasts point the finger at owner Jerry Jones. With a 3-5 record, the Cowboys aren’t out of the race, as the NFC East is still up for grabs. It will be interesting to see who the finger is pointed at

item.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
item.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. In an afternoon keynote moderated by Marlene Ogawa of Synergos, Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa , South Africa CEO of Naspers, and Gareth Ackerman, Non-Executive Director at Pick n Pay, kept things practical: back women entrepreneurs without taking equity, start with your own family and community, use local distributors, and make it easier to travel between African countries. One retraining program they discussed moved 7,200 of 8,000 university graduates into tech jobs. The difference between charity and philanthropy, they said, is helping people help themselves. item.description: 'Nee po mone Dinesha': Sachin Tendulkar drops Mohanlal's iconic dialogue when asked about Sanju Samson originally appeared on Cricket News . He had only a sentence as an answer but used an iconic Malayalam dialogue from the legendary actor Mohanlal's film "Narasimham." The Master Blaster told a fan that the CSK batter would explain the meaning of his cheeky response. If you are unsure about receiving a reply from Sanju on this matter, don't worry! Worry not, we've got you covered! Sanju Samson had turned to Sachin Tendulkar during his toughest T20 World Cup phase Sachin's response also brought back memories of the guidance he offered Sanju during a difficult phase ahead of the 2026 T20 World Cup. item.title: Rays excercise option for Taylor Walls
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 26: Taylor Walls #6 of the Tampa Bay Rays takes the field during player introductions prior to Game Three of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, October 26, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Last offseason, the Rays had a club option for Taylor Walls. There was some uncertainty at the time if the Rays would choose to go with Walls for the 2026 campaign with Carson Williams seemingly ready to take over. But not only did the Rays accept their option on Walls, but the two sides agreed to a deal that added an option for the 2027 season. The Rays faced the exact same situation entering this offseason and have chosen to excercise Walls’ 2027 option. Thus paying him $3.1M for the 2027 campaign; MLB Trade Rumors projected Walls to receive $3.5M in what would have been his final year of arbitration eligibility. The 30-year old switch-hitting Walls provided the Rays with exactly what they expected as he hit .222/.309/.298 with 2 HR over 433 PA. The 74 wRC+ he finished the season with was his highest offensive output since the 2023 campaign where he finished the year with a 84 wRC+. It’s not the offense that had Walls as the Rays starting shortstop in the World Series though, it’s his defense which is among the best in all of baseball. Among shorstops all-time on FanGraphs with at least 2000 innings played, Walls ranks 9th in DRS. The baseball world took notice as Walls was finally awarded a Gold Glove award after his third career nomination.

item.title: Police open investigation into death of footballer after on-field collision
item.description: Police in Spain have confirmed they have opened a “routine” investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died in hospital on Tuesday after suffering a cardiac arrest as a result of a collision during a match on Monday. De Miguel, 30, collapsed on the pitch after a clash with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who had rushed out of his area to clear the ball but struck the forward in the chest. The match was then abandoned and Owono was shown a red card following the incident, which took place in stoppage time of the second division fixture. De Miguel was taken to hospital after receiving treatment on the pitch. Tenerife initially reported that he was “stable, despite the severity of his condition” before reporting that his neurological condition had worsened in the early hours of Tuesday. They confirmed his death at around 8am on Tuesday. Tenerife's Jesus de Miguel in action against FC Andorra (Reuters) While Spain’s National Police said prosecutors would be involved, authorities in the Canary Islands said the opening of an investigation into the footballer’s death was a routine procedure. Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry. In a statement, Tenerife said: “Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, we at CD Tenerife announce the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda. There are no words of comfort. There is absolutely nothing that can ease this overwhelming sense of sadness.” Owono, a Equatorial Guinea international, has deactivated his Instagram account since the incident. A statement from Andorra read: “With broken hearts, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.” Several Spanish teams, including Barcelona and Real Madrid, paid tribute, while Fifpro, the world players’ union, said: “Fifpro is deeply saddened by the passing of CD Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel. Our thoughts are with Jesus’ family, friends, team-mates, everyone at CD Tenerife, and all those affected. Rest in peace, Jesus.” FC Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel is carried on a stretcher (AP) La Liga president Javier Tebas expressed his shock and said the league would work to support the club and De Miguel’s family, and said he would speak to Tenerife about potentially postponing their next match out of concern for the players’ welfare. Speaking in an interview with Television Canaria, Tebas also raised the possibility of a joint tribute between La Liga and the Segunda Division. Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin said: “We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda. We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his team-mates, everyone at Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss.” All Uefa matches this week will be preceded with a

item.title: Police investigate Spanish striker’s death after on-pitch collision with goalkeeper
item.description: Spain’s National Police have launched an investigation into the death of CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel following his collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, with the case now under judicial supervision. Sources at the provincial police headquarters confirmed the development to AFP. De Miguel, 30, died at Nuestra Señora de La Candelaria Hospital, hours after sustaining serious injuries in a collision with Owono during Monday’s match at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium. “Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 am (0700 GMT), of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,” his club Tenerife said in a statement. “No words can ease the pain, nothing can lessen this great feeling of sadness. Our thoughts are with the family, his close friends and Tenerife fans, who today are grieving over this terrible news.” The incident occurred in second-half stoppage time, with the score tied at 2-2, as the Tenerife striker chased an aerial ball beyond the halfway line. Spanish media said that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated. The player was taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, with Tenerife later saying that De Miguel’s condition had “worsened neurologically”, before his death. The post Police investigate Spanish striker’s death after on-pitch collision with goalkeeper appeared first on Vanguard News .

Some clubs will hunt for solid starting pitching, while others just need more pop and reliable bats in their lineup. This winter’s market has a little bit of everything, older veterans, young stars and guys with proven track records. Good talent is out there at almost every spot, from the rotation to the infield, outfield and behind the plate. What each player gets will come down to simple things: how much money they want, how healthy they’ve stayed, their age and how well they played lately. MORE: Yankees linked to biggest slugger on MLB free agent market A few top names will definitely get chased by contenders hoping to make a deep playoff run. Other players might make more sense for rebuilding teams looking ahead. Either way, with this much talent on the table, the 2026 offseason could shake things up all across the league. item.title: Woman, 24, Dies from Rare Muscle Condition After Collapsing 2 Miles from Finish Line of New York City Marathon
item.description: Rachel Apa Credit: Rachel Apa/Instagram NEED TO KNOW Rachel Apa, 24, died after collapsing during the New York City Marathon, which she was running in memory of her grandfather, on Sunday, Nov. 1 Spectators gave her CPR, before medical staff used a defibrillator and paramedics transported her to the hospital, where she was later pronounced dead Her father, Steve Apa, said she died from the rare condition rhabdomyolysis, in which the muscles break down and poison the body A 24-year-old woman who was running the New York City Marathon in memory of her grandfather died after collapsing just two miles from the finish line. Rachel Apa, from Lewisberry, Pa., was in Central Park, near the 24th mile mark, at about 1:30 p.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1, when she collapsed, The New York Times reported. Spectators, some of whom said they were physicians, ran over and gave Rachel CPR before medical staff arrived and used a defibrillator. Central Park during the New York City Marathon on Nov. 1, 2026 Credit: Ishika Samant/Getty Paramedics arrived and took her to the nearby Mount Sinai Medical Center in an ambulance, with her mom, Michelle Apa, traveling in a second ambulance to be by her side, her dad, Steve Apa, told the Times . Despite doctors’ efforts to save her life, Rachel was declared dead at about 9:40 p.m. Her parents had been tracking her progress, and at the 14th mile, Michelle took a video of her daughter high-fiving toward the camera, while Steve was at home in Lewisberry tracking her on the marathon app and texting her at every mile. At the 18th mile, she replied, “Ow,” and then “Ow ow,” a mile later, the Times reported. Her dad continued texting, but didn’t receive any further replies. Runners in the New York City Marathon on Nov. 1, 2026 Credit: Theodore Parisienne / New York Daily News via Getty Steve told the newspaper she died from rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition in which the muscles break down and poison the body. Per Cleveland Clinic , rhabdomyolysis is often brought on by excessive exercise or injury, and can be life-threatening. “It’s unfathomable,” he said. “Perfect health, perfect shape, 24 years old.” Rachel, who played field hockey at Bucknell University in Lewisburg, Pa., and had recently started a master’s degree program at Charleston Southern University in North Charleston, S.C., was running her first marathon to raise money in memory of her grandfather, who died from Parkinson’s disease four years ago. “My grandfather was my role model growing up. He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges, shaping my love for sports and movement,” she wrote on her Parkinson’s Champions fundraising page. item.title: RFL backs Wilkin's £30m funding plea to Burnham
item.description: Jon Wilkin played 10 times for England between 2004 and 2011, and six times for Great Britain in 2006 and 2007 [Getty Images] The new head of English rugby league has backed a call for Prime Minister Andy Burnham to approve a £30m five-year community funding plan for the sport. Former England international Jon Wilkin has appealed directly to Burnham and Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy, both rugby league fans, to pledge government money to a rugby league-based social impact project. Ian Nolan, the new chief executive of the Rugby Football League, has supported Wilkin's plea, issued on BBC Radio 5 Live's Rugby League show on Monday. Wilkin wants Burnham and Nandy to follow the lead of Australia's government, which in July announced it was committing A$250m (£130m) over 10 years to the Pacific Rugby League Partnership. That initiative is designed to help create sporting, educational and employment opportunities in Papua New Guinea, Tonga, Samoa and Fiji, and is being led by the Australian Rugby League Commission - the country's rugby league governing body. Wilkin has argued that a similar plan for the north of England would benefit deprived communities. He said: "Australia has recognised rugby league's potential as a vehicle for social change, committing hundreds of millions to developing communities, especially across the Pacific. Why shouldn't Britain show the same ambition for the north? "The infrastructure already exists, the clubs, the foundations, the school and community relationships are already well established. What's missing is a coordinated strategy and meaningful government investment. "The ask would be simple: For the government to establish a £30m five-year Northern Rugby League social impact partnership, bringing together the RFL, professional clubs, community foundations, local authorities and government departments. "The programme would target disadvantaged northern communities." Nolan, a former Manchester United executive who took up his role with the RFL on 1 October, suggested the social benefits of such an initiative would be felt more quickly because rugby league clubs are already established in their communities. "When the government normally invest in community hubs and new things to generate something, they tend to be brand new," he said. "And it's really difficult then to attract people to go there because it's a new habit, it's a new place. "But rugby clubs are already established in the most deprived towns in the UK. And that's the difference. People already go there. Families already rely on them for even just moving around." BBC Sport has contacted the Department for Culture, Media and Sport for comment. 'A big opportunity to start a new Ashes-type series' Nolan announced on Sunday that the RFL will be consulting English rugby league greats to map out a future for the national game under an initiative it is calling One Game, One England. item.title: NFL Panic Meter: With other contenders making big trades, the Rams have to figure out a way to keep up
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams pushed a lot of chips to the middle of the table over the offseason. Then, when they came out of the gates slow, other teams saw an opportunity. Last week, the Seattle Seahawks made a big move for guard Quenton Nelson and the San Francisco 49ers got a big acquisition in defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. The NFC West got a lot harder. The Chicago Bears, clearly believing the NFC is up for grabs, traded a couple first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . His stellar play on Monday night in his Bears debut has lifted Chicago's ceiling for this season. Other top NFC teams will inevitably add to their rosters. The Rams need to look to see if they have any more chips remaining to up their bet. Head coach Sean McVay says the Rams aren't likely to be buyers. He says the team is content to have key players who have been on injured reserve, like defensive end Myles Garrett and wideout Davante Adams, provide the boost that a trade deadline acquisition normally would. "The amount of guys that have not been available, that are key and focal points for really both sides of the football, you look at those guys hopefully being able to return within a month," McVay said, according to the Los Angeles Times , "and that's kind of where that value lies for us."' Given the Rams' history, and how aggressive they were in the offseason leading up to this season, that's difficult to believe. Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay and his team got off to a rough start but are back to .500. AP Photo/Caroline Brehman The Rams are already committed. They made huge trades for cornerback Trent McDuffie and Garrett, and also added a big signing with cornerback Jaylen Watson. They have already traded draft picks in the first, fifth and sixth rounds this year, in the first and third in 2027, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. There's no turning back now. And they're looking to make big deals at anytime, even in years they weren't big preseason Super Bowl favorites. The Rams' 2-4 start was stunning. Garrett underwent knee surgery and there have been few updates on a timetable for his return. Then they suffered an injury to a position that was already perilously thin, when Adams injured his hamstring. He's out for six to 10 weeks, and there's no guarantee a player who turns 34 years old in December rebounds from an injury like that. The Rams can mask the injury with a lot of three tight end sets and running the ball more, but they won't be the same explosive offense from a season ago. The need at receiver beyond Puka Nacua is glaring. The Rams are 4-4 after a couple straight wins, which keeps them in the NFC race, but their .500 record and the activity around the NFC West is a reminder that there's still a gap they need to close. Perhaps that occurs through the star players that will return from injury, though that's tough to depend on. Or maybe the Rams decide that now isn't the time to stop trading. Pa

item.title: Florida State women’s basketball overwhelms Merrimack in season opener
item.description: Florida State women’s basketball opened its 2026-27 season with an 81-51 victory over the Merrimack College Warriors on Monday at the Donald L. Tucker Civic Center. After leading by one point through the first quarter, the Seminoles took control with a 22-4 second quarter. FSU followed that stretch with a 29-9 third quarter, turning a competitive opener into a 39-point advantage entering the final 10 minutes. Freshman guard Morgan Stewart led the scoring with 13 points and four steals, while senior guard Solé Williams and junior guard Tatum Greene added 11 points apiece. “We had great defense in spurts and that really, I thought, spurred our offense on,” head coach Brooke Wyckoff said in the postgame press conference. Defensive surge reshapes the opening half Merrimack scored first, but fifth-year guard Timaya Lewis-Eutsey answered for the ’Noles. Neither team managed to gain much separation in the first quarter, as the Warriors stayed within reach after the opening media timeout. The period ended 16-15 in favor of the Garnet and Gold. Never miss a beat: Sign up for the FSView Newsletter That changed in the second. Florida State disrupted possessions, pressured ballhandlers, and converted defensive stops into scoring chances. Sophomore guard Mari Gerton recorded a steal, and Greene made a layup with roughly 3:30 remaining in the half as the margin widened. The Seminoles held Merrimack to four points in the period, compared with 15 in the first. By halftime, the score had moved to 38-19, with the Warriors unable to match FSU’s defensive intensity. "Our plan was to wear them down over the course of the game," Wyckoff said. "Once we kind of got our footing in the second quarter, [we] just turned up our defensive intensity and pressure." Wyckoff explained that Merrimack’s spacing and perimeter shooting created challenges for the ’Noles early, but once the Garnet and Gold found their footing in the second quarter, they turned up their defensive intensity and pressure. The turnovers began to pile up: the Warriors finished with 34, while Florida State recorded 18 steals and 45 points off turnovers. The Seminoles also grabbed 14 offensive rebounds and held a 48-26 advantage in points in the paint. Williams finds her rhythm after halftime FSU scored first out of the break, pushing the advantage to 42-19. The team extended it to 50-26 and later 65-26, continuing to capitalize on Merrimack’s mistakes. Williams scored nine of her 11 points in the third quarter after contributing two in the first half. Her burst helped the ’Noles turn a substantial halftime lead into a one-sided contest. "I was kind of quiet in the first half, and then I just knew like, I got to continue to just show up for my team," Williams said in the postgame press conference. By the end of the quarter, the Garnet and Gold led 67-28. Their largest advantage reached 41 points before Merrimack won the fourth quarter, 23-14. item.title: Osun APC backtracks, renames ‘parallel’ list as parliamentary campaign committee
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Following protest from members and rejection of a parallel presidential campaign committee by the national leadership, the Osun State All Progressives Congress (APC) has renamed its earlier presidential/parliamentary campaign committee to just the parliamentary campaign committee. The Osun APC in statement signed by the Party Chairman on Monday had released a parallel presidential campaign committee list which has the Governorship candidate as its Director-General after the Presidential Campaign Council Coordinator, Governor Ademola Adeleke, had inaugurated a campaign committee in the state. However, three members of the State Executive Committee, Wole Adunola, State Publicity Secretary; Adesola Ayangbile, Welfare Officer; and Rasheed Adeniji, Asst. Organising Secretary, and Abiola Ololade, Ex-Officio, in a joint statement, rejected the list on the ground that it does not reflect due process and lacked inclusiveness. This reportedly led to the national leadership of the party rejecting the said campaign committee list. Meanwhile, the APC, in another statement issued by the party chairman, Tajudeen Lawal, on Tuesday, renamed the list as parliamentary campaign committee, retaining the party’s governorship candidate in the August 15 election as the Director-General. The statement attached to the list reads, “Following the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) by the national leader of our party and its presidential candidate, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, on the 14th of October 2026 in Abuja, and the subsequent inauguration of the Osun State PCC by the Executive Governor of Osun State, His Excellency, Governor Ademola Nurudeen Jackson Adeleke, on the 22nd of October 2026, we consider it extremely important to therefore bolster the efforts of the PCC to deliver massive votes for the reelection of our President, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (GCFR) in the forthcoming general elections.” “We have therefore carefully selected out All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders and members in Osun State to actualise our collective desire of ensuring a round victory for the President as well as our National and State Assembly candidates. “As a party, we are resolute to work in unison with every member of the State Presidential Campaign to deliver on our mandate as we muster concerted efforts to ensure victory for all the National and State Assemblies candidates of our great party,” it added. The post Osun APC backtracks, renames ‘parallel’ list as parliamentary campaign committee appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Who is goalkeeper Jesus Owono and will he be punished after Miguel’s death?
item.description: Jesus Owono has become a global figure overnight after the goalkeeper’s challenge led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel. The 30-year-old died in hospital in Santa Cruz on Tuesday morning after suffering a cardiac arrest in the wake of a high challenge by Andorra goalkeeper Owono in stoppage time of Monday’s La Liga 2 game. Owono received a straight red card for his challenge and has since received criticism from around the world for his part in the tragedy while local police are reported to have begun an investigation into the incident, CD Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel collides with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a football match in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Spain, on November 2, 2026 [Sergio Mendez/Diario de Avisos via AP Photo] Who is Jesus Owono? The 25-year-old goalkeeper was born in Bata, Equatorial Guinea, but moved to Spain’s Basque Country as a child. His first club was Antiguoko, a youth club in San Sebastian, at the age of eight, but after moving on to Real Sociedad, he played for the Basque Country’s representative side at under-16 level. He joined Alaves in 2017 and worked his way through the youth ranks before making his first-team debut in a 1-1 draw against Real Sociedad in January 2022, becoming the first international born in his country to appear in La Liga. He went on to make 20 appearances in the league and Copa del Rey but spent last season on loan with La Liga 2 side Andorra, keeping six clean sheets in 20 league games before earning a permanent move in August and signing a two-year deal. Owono made his Equatorial Guinea debut shortly after turning 18 in March 2019 and has gone on to represent his country 46 times, playing every minute of their three group games in the 2025 AFCON edition and both their AFCON 2027 qualifiers against DR Congo and Sierra Leone in September. How did Owono react to the collision? After colliding with De Miguel in the centre circle, Owono did not turn back to look at his opponent on the ground but immediately began walking towards the touchline, anticipating the red card which Manuel Angel Perez Hernandez swiftly brandished. However, as he walked off, after exchanging a handshake with teammate Nacho Quintana, he turned back as medical staff were beckoned frantically onto the pitch and jogged to join players surrounding De Miguel as he lay prostrate on the turf. He remained on the field until he was led away by club officials and down the tunnel at the same time that De Miguel was being rushed off the field at the opposite end of the stadium on a stretcher to a waiting ambulance, with videos posted online showing Tenerife fans in the stands chanting ‘assassin’ at Owono for his part in the incident. Why has Owono received online abuse? The reaction to Owono’s challenge on De Miguel is that it was widely considered reckless and using excessive force. The keeper was standing well outside his area as 10-man Andorra piled on late pressure, seeking to complete an unlikely comeback

item.title: William Saliba returns to Arsenal training
item.description: LONDON COLNEY, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 03: William Saliba of Arsenal during the training session on day ahead of the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 at on November 03, 2026 in London Colney, England. (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images) | Arsenal FC via Getty Images Folks, it happened. William Saliba is back in Arsenal training. The French centerback has been out of action since the World Cup semifinal recovering from a back injury that the club knew would need addressing after last season. Saliba, presumably with the input and blessing of the club and the French National Team doctors, decided that he’d manage his injury through the tournament and deal with the back issue afterwards. Early in that semifinal, he went down, could be seen saying “my back is gone” to his teammates, and that was that. The “good” post-World Cup news was that Saliba would not need surgery to repair the problem. But he did need several months of rest and rehabilitation to heal. The exact nature of his injury was never disclosed, just that it was a “longstanding” problem. My suspicion is that he had a fractured vertebrae. I had one about 25 years ago and Saliba’s ability to manage the injury and continue playing for a time, suddenly being unable to keep playing through it, treatment plan, and length of absence match up with my experience. Mikel Arteta told reporters that Saliba is scheduled for another MRI next week to check on the “healing process” so it doesn’t sound as if he is quite ready for action. For what it’s worth, Saliba was said to be aiming for a November return to action, and the initial timelines suggested Arsenal might not have him back until December. Either way, his return to training is excellent news. William Saliba is one of the best, if not the best, CB in the world. Whenever he gets back on the pitch for Arsenal, it’ll make the team better. And that’s saying something because the Gunners have the best defensive record in the Premier League, in large part due to Ezri Konsa’s nearly seamlessly slotting into Saliba’s place. Mikel Arteta will having some rotation and pairings stuff to work out, but that’s a brilliant problem to have. Welcome (mostly) back, Wilo!

item.description: SOUTH BEND, IN - OCTOBER 23: Fans are seen tailgating before the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and USC Trojans game at Notre Dame Stadium on October 23, 2021 in South Bend, Indiana. In fact, it’s the biggest game FOR Notre Dame and quite possibly their opponent as well, the Miami Hurricanes. As we’ve talked about in the past, on of the fun things to see in November is when southern warm-weather schools are forced to travel north to play a game. How cold will it be? Will it snow? Will the southern team be slowed down by the entire catalog of the North Face brand? Well… it ain’t like that at all this weekend. Tailgaters are going to enjoy spectacular weather all day long as they grill and drink the day away surrounded by peak fall foliage. After a warmer than usual week, fans will get a high of around 51 degrees under a partly sunny sky. That forecast, however, is just for the fans. What about the weather at game time? How cold will it get once that sun drops down on the western horizon? Well… it’s fall football weather. item.title: 4 Arsenal players make shortlist for FIFPRO Men’s World 11
item.description: 4 Arsenal players make shortlist for FIFPRO Men’s World 11 Four Arsenal players have made the final shortlist of 26 players in contention to make the FIFAPRO Men’s World 11, with the team to be revealed next week. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images FIFPRO have revealed their 26-player shortlist for their Men’s World 11, after tallying up the votes from 19,806 professional footballers from 73 countries. The 26 players on the shortlist are those who received the most votes from their peers for their performances from August 2025 to July 2026. The 11 players with the most votes in their respective positions will then make the final team. That team will be revealed on Monday, November 9th at 16:00 GMT, with four Arsenal players in contention to feature in it. Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images David Raya is one of just three goalkeepers to make the cut, competing with Thibaut Courtois and Emi Martinez . Funnily enough, recent Yashin Trophy winner Unai Simon didn’t make the cut on this occasion. Whilst the FIFPRO World 11 is voted on by professional footballers, the Yashin Trophy is voted on by journalists. But Raya can perhaps take some encouragement from the results of the Yashin Trophy vote, given he significantly outperformed Courtois and Martinez and only finished second to his international teammate Simon. Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images For Premier League In defence, Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba are among just five centre-backs on the shortlist, joining Pau Cubarsi , Virgil van Dijk , and Dayot Upamecano . Then Declan Rice is one of a relatively long list of central midfielders, joining Jude Bellingham , Bruno Fernandes , Enzo Fernandez , Pedri , Rodri , and Vitinha . But it’s likely three spots will be up for grabs, so the England international still has a chance. Any of the four players would be deserving entrants in the World 11, and we’ll find out next Monday if any of them have made the cut. Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images

item.title: Key refereeing changes explained as rugby’s Nations Championship returns
item.description: Top referees will clamp down on scrummaging technique in a bid to stabilise the set-piece during November’s Nations Championship fixtures as World Rugby seeks greater alignment in officiating across the sport. Match officials in the 12-team competition, and the Nations Cup which sits beneath it, have been provided with specialist input from figures including former Wales captain Jon Humphreys and Warren Gatland to refine and clarify their processes. Of particular focus will be on loosehead props ensuring they do not show a “tucked” right shoulder, with front rows encouraged to be temple-to-temple on engagement and ensure space is provided to tightheads to scrummage. The importance of the brake foot has also been emphasised in keeping players safe, while officials have also been asked to only reward teams who establish their dominance in a straight line, rather than at an angle. There was significant discussion around the scrum during South Africa and New Zealand’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, with officials keen to preserve the contest as a key battleground. All 24 head coaches were invited into World Rugby’s officiating camp to meet with decision-makers with a year to go until the World Cup, both with a view to ensuring clarity ahead of November and with a longer-term view towards the shape of the game. The governing body’s data shows that ball in play time in matches featuring the world’s top 12 nations has swelled by more than two minutes since 2024, with stoppages down 10 per cent. The average number of tries per game has increased from 6.3 to 8.2, with successful penalty kicks falling from 3.5 to 1.5 in a sign of an evolving sport. Changes in the kick-to-pass ratio also suggest that teams are more willing to play a greater number of phases with ball-in-hand. Top referees have met with international coaches ahead of the Nations Championship (Getty) Coaches are understood to have been relatively happy with the officiating of the breakdown, though World Rugby has moved to refine its head contact process to make decision-making clearer in that area. Mitigating factors such as a late change in dynamics will be considered provided a player arrives in control and attempting a legal clearout even if head contact is made. Teams have also been provided with detail on the implementation of the “knee-drop” and “hip-drop” tackle laws . The latter of these will draw stiffer sanction should a player fall directly on the legs of a ball carrier having made a tackle from behind given the risk of serious injury. A challenge of this type made with significant force will be punished with a 20-minute red card. An example of a knee-drop tackle (Getty) A knee-drop tackle fails to stay on their feet before making a tackle, placing a knee on the floor. It will generally be sanctioned with just a penalty, and is unlikely to be strictly enforced around the try line as defensive players attempt to stay low and prevent the ball being grounded. item.title: Harvick: NASCAR may penalize Hocevar for 'dirtiest of dirty tricks'
item.description: Motorsport photo Kevin Harvick says Carson Hocevar has placed NASCAR in a bit of a complicated bind this week due to the aggressive brake checking that knocked Austin Cindric out of the Cup Series race at Martinsville Speedway on Sunday. The 2014 Cup Series champion turned FOX analyst believes NASCAR will need to look at this in the same light as an intentional right rear hook. The comments were made on Monday during his weekly show with IndyCar play-by-play voice Will Buxton. Read Also: Data reveals severity of Carson Hocevar's brake-check: "There's no denying it" Jeff Burton and Dale Jarrett blast Carson Hocevar: "That's not racing" “Yeah, usually you hold that for your worst enemies,” said Harvick on the show. “Been there, done that with the brake-check thing. And usually that is leading to the last source of, ‘Hey, middle finger, I don’t care what you think. I’m going to I’m going to tear your day up.’ “And as I went back and watched all these videos, I just, ah, man, there wasn’t a lot of contact from the 2 car, leaning on the back bumper. And then you saw what he did to Austin Cindric and the three or four brake-checks. “So, you know, it’s an interesting scenario that it has put NASCAR in, because, as I said, I’ve been in this scenario where you use that method. But usually, it’s where you’re completely mad at a situation or a person to be able to cause a war. And, you know, there was no war afterwards. “But, you know, with the way that they’ve softened the front of these cars up and the things that have happened to the front bumpers over the course of this season to keep the drivers from having the impacts that they had. I think it’s definitely something that, as a driver, when you have that in your tool bag, I know what I held that for.” Read Also: Carson Hocevar denies intent in Austin Cindric clash: “We were just having fun” Drivers believe softer bumpers will impact NASCAR Cup race at Martinsville Harvick is referencing the decision by NASCAR made earlier in the year to make the front bumpers even softer -- that even the slightest of contact would cave them in. The reasons were one part safety and one part competitive, but two drivers weaponized this on Sunday. Josh Berry gave a brake check to Ryan Blaney but Hocevar very aggressively over the course of multiple laps used his back bumper to retire the Team Penske No.2 from the race. In real time, spotter Tyler Green kept telling Hocevar to stop brake checking Cindric, and that went ignored. Thus, Harvick says NASCAR needs to explore a penalty on Hocevar, whom is already under a kind of loose probation period as he’s already been called into the series hauler this season too. “I think when you look at it from a NASCAR standpoint, it’s detrimental to the way that you want to see things race and probably falls into the right-rear hook category of whether it’s intentional or not intentional with the way that all this happens. “That’s the dirtiest of dirty tricks that you can possibly use o

item.title: FG laying solid AI foundation for businesses to thrive – Tijan
item.description: Dr Bosun Tijani, the Minister of Communication and Digital Economy says the Federal Government is laying the foundation for Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption in Nigeria. Tijani said this at the Oxford Global Think Tank (OGTT), where he identified private sector investment as essential to translating government-led reforms into jobs, businesses and wider economic opportunities. ‎He said though government could provide infrastructure, policy direction and an enabling environment, businesses should develop products and services that would translate those investments into economic value. ‎“Government can do reform, invest in foundation for AI but it is businesses that will build the growth on top of those foundations,” he said. The minister outlined five essential foundations for countries seeking to benefit from AI. “One is connectivity, second is compute and data infrastructure, third is data, fourth is skills and research capability and lastly, policy and institutions,” he said. ‎He said Nigeria was investing two billion dollars in an open-access fibre-optic network spanning 90,000 kilometres to expand broadband connectivity across the country. Tijani also said that government was establishing shared computing capacity for researchers, developing local AI capabilities and pursuing a target of training three million technical talents. He said Nigeria had also developed a government-backed large language model capable of communicating in Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, Ibibio and accented English. The minister cited the telecommunications sector as evidence of how government reforms could create opportunities for private businesses, recalling how liberalisation in 2001 attracted investment and expanded access to mobile services. He said the telecommunications expansion created opportunities in financial technology, commerce, logistics and other sectors. Tijani said Nigeria should approach AI with similar collaboration between government, businesses and knowledge institutions. ‎“Our responsibilities as leaders is to build the capacity through which extraordinary possibilities of technology become ordinary improvements in people’s lives,” he said. ‎Arunma Oteh, Convener of OGTT, says Africa should take an active role in shaping the future of AI to avoid being left behind in the emerging technology. Oteh said the platform focused on inclusive prosperity, addressing inequalities and harnessing Africa’s potential through thought leadership and practical action. ‎“We believe that technology is an amplifier; that leveraging technology is critical to prosperity because it brings skill. ‎”We are cognisant of the dangers of technology but we think that those can be managed, she said. Dr Chidinma Okolo, Project Delivery Manager, Space & Satellite Applications Sector said Africa’s challenge in AI was not a lack of talent but ownership of the technology and the economic value it generates. item.title: AI & Equity: The Big Conversations at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026
item.description: The Goalkeepers 2026 Event in Dakar brought together innovators, global leaders and experts on how AI can be further leveraged by Africans for an equitable future On October 29, 2026, Africans gathered in Dakar, Senegal, to discuss the continent’s relationship with the world’s fastest-growing technology: artificial intelligence (AI). This event was part of the Goalkeepers 2026 series and was themed “Make This Matter: Equitable AI and the Future of African Youth .” It brought together professionals and innovators who focused on how Africa can adopt AI to fill gaps and ensure equitable access across various sectors . Africans are leveraging AI for business, education and more, but as AI continues to develop and expand rapidly, it is crucial for us to use it on a bigger scale, ensuring collective development and an equitable future for all. This makes the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar particularly significant. Nigerian influencer, Saskay, at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026 The event included several activities, including performances from the legendary Youssou N’Dour , a Qui veut changer le monden session where people pitched their ideas, conversations about AI and equity and more. Here are some of the major talking points at the event: AI and Existing Solutions The event was graciously hosted in English and French by Fatou Jupiter Toure , who opened by sharing a powerful African message: “It is not about what you can do. It is about what we can do for each other.” Despite the diverse cultures and beliefs that exist on the continent, Africans have remained held by the belief of “I am because you are.” This is why, despite AI’s fast growth, Africans are coming together to examine how much it concerns them, how it can be properly leveraged and what dangers and challenges lie ahead. Fatou Jupiter Toure hosting the Goalkeepers 2026 event in Dakar Nevertheless, Africans have done a great deal of work with AI. Innovators have used AI tools to provide solutions in their local communities. Vyonne Njeri shared how she got into healthcare and how AI has been greatly helping in the community she serves. In the Goalkeepers 2026 Report , Vyonne said she got into healthcare during a visit to see her uncle, a priest in a small, East Kenyan town called Modogashe. She highlighted that even though AI greatly supports her work, she remains the clinical officer. She explained that “AI is not perfect. It must not take over clinical work. But it can help us share across accessible healthcare. It can help discover what could have been missed early. We still need people to be trained, but AI tools can greatly support us.” Like Vyonne, Mamadou Ly also shared why and how AI can aid learning, especially in local languages. He said, “Education is not just about reading and writing. It is also an act of dignity.” Mamadou Ly at Goalkeepers Dakar 2026. item.title: Iran president says return to war benefits ‘no one’, after reported US strikes
item.description: Iran’s president Masoud Pezeshkian said on Tuesday that a return to war would benefit “no one”, hours after reported US strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz. It came as US voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump’s grip on power. Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Islamic republic was “ready for battle with its finger on the trigger”, while deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran retained the right to “legitimate self-defence” after the strikes. But Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis “through dialogue”, adding that “no one will benefit from this war” if it reignited, and emphasising that the country’s supreme leader had recently granted the government new powers to negotiate issues previously “off-limits”. The US strikes, reported by The Wall Street Journal, CNN, The New York Times and other outlets, hit Qeshm island in the Hormuz waterway, a key flashpoint of the Middle East war that has upended global markets. Unnamed US officials cited by the outlets described the attacks as defensive in nature. The Journal said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes. US Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment. – ‘Iran wants a settlement’ – The US and Israel launched their war with Iran with a massive wave of strikes in late February. The conflict has been stalemated for months. Asked if Israel was involved in the latest reported strikes, an Israeli military spokesperson told AFP, “No”. The reported Qeshm attack came just hours after Trump signalled a deal with Iran “could happen”, as US voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterms dominated by public dissatisfaction with the war and the inflation it has brought. “Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies. Ghalibaf said the ball was in Washington’s court. “The countries of the region should know that, just as the Islamic Republic of Iran stands ready for battle with its finger on the trigger, it has also given the American side a powerful and rational response,” he said in a televised speech. “The ball is now in America’s court to prevent war.” – ‘Committed’ – Qatar, a mediator in protracted indirect negotiations between the US and Iran, said it remained hopeful of an interim deal in the war. “Both parties remain committed to the negotiation process; as we mentioned, we are facilitating the real-time exchange of proposals between them,” foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters. Both sides “are currently reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented,” he added. “We remain hopeful that there is still a chance for a deal to take place,” he said, adding Doha was workin

item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $77,500 as Midterm Voting Begins
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $77,500 as Midterm Voting Begins Bitcoin price traded near $77,500 on Tuesday morning as polls opened for the U.S. midterm elections, down about .6% on the day and roughly $30,000 below its price one year ago, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The vote decides control of Congress and, with it, the fate of the CLARITY Act, the market structure bill that passed the House 294-134 in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15. Prediction markets on Kalshi give Democrats a 94% chance of taking the House and 74% for the Senate. A Democratic Senate would likely put Sen. Elizabeth Warren in line to chair the Banking Committee. If Congress does not act before the new session convenes on Jan. 3, the bill dies and must be reintroduced. Crypto groups spent more than $200 million on the midterms, CNBC reported. Analysts at TD Cowen see a Democratic sweep as the most probable outcome and the least favorable one for the industry; a divided Congress, in their view, leaves room for a narrower deal. A week of selling The bitcoin price action into the vote has been one-directional. Bitcoin price opened November near $78,500 and has lost about $2,000 since. October closed down about 7%, the second straight October decline. On Oct. 28, after a hawkish Federal Reserve hold and weak earnings from Alphabet and Samsung, the price fell below $80,000 for the first time in weeks, with about $356 million in leveraged positions liquidated. The larger shock came the next day. On Oct. 29, attackers the FBI attributes to North Korea drained about $6.3 billion from Binance’s hot wallets, the largest crypto theft on record. Bitcoin price held strong but fell about 4% on Friday and more than $1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $643.3 million that day, their largest single-day outflow since June 25, according to SoSoValue data. Another $399 million left on Monday. Bitcoin recovered to $78,491 late Sunday before sliding again on Monday and Tuesday. The 50-day EMA near $80,800 is the first resistance above. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 37 on Monday, in “fear” territory. item.title: Drax wants to feed Britain's AI habit with £20B datacenter at biomass power station
item.description: Britain's AI infrastructure boom could soon have an unlikely new home: Drax Power Station, where the operator of the country's largest biomass power plant has unveiled plans for a £20 billion datacenter development capable of consuming more than a gigawatt of power. Drax announced on Tuesday that it has teamed up with investment giant Brookfield and its UK-based AI infrastructure business Radiant to build the facility at its North Yorkshire site. The money would come through a joint venture between Brookfield and Qatar's Qai, although the £20 billion headline figure is more ambition than actual money on the table at this stage. The companies plan to start relatively small, at least by the standards of the AI industry's apparently bottomless appetite for electricity. The first phase would deliver up to 100MW of capacity by early 2028, backed by a proposed £2.5 billion investment. A second phase could add another 500MW between 2028 and 2031, with further expansion taking the site beyond 1GW after that. However, a few hurdles remain between today's announcement and a functioning AI megafactory. According to Drax's regulatory filing , the first phase still requires planning permission, regulatory and network approvals, commercial agreements, and final investment decisions. It also needs a tenant, which is a fairly important detail when you're proposing to spend billions on somewhere to house other people's computers. Drax reckons its existing infrastructure gives it an advantage over developers struggling to secure electricity connections. The 1,000-acre site already has access to 4GW of grid capacity, 2.6GW of active generation and cooling infrastructure, along with proximity to the UK's fiber network. The UK government estimated last week that all of Britain's existing data centers use around 2GW of electricity. Drax's proposed development alone could eventually need more than 1GW, although how much power it actually consumes will depend on how fully it's used. The first phase would draw electricity from the grid, but Drax wants to supply up to 500MW directly from its existing generating capacity under a long-term power purchase agreement, potentially allowing AI servers to run on electricity produced by burning imported wood pellets. That brings another complication. Drax signed a government-backed Contract for Difference agreement last year covering biomass generation between April 2027 and March 2031. The agreement allows the company to request permission to redirect up to 500MW of capacity towards a datacenter, but ministers and the Low Carbon Contracts Company would have to agree, taking into account consumer value, energy security, and sustainability. The announcement also arrives as enthusiasm for enormous AI server farms is proving rather less universal outside government and industry circles.
